BBC News, 16 November 2026

Ex-PM Johnson says 'Britain would back Brexit again' and 'zero hours ban to cost billions'

Front page of the Times with the headline \"Zero-hours ban to cost billions\" and Daily Telegraph with the headline \"Johnson: Britain would back Brexit again\"

The Daily Telegraph reports that former Prime Minister Boris Johnson believes \"Britain would back Brexit\" a second time if Andy Burnham forces anther vote on the issue. On Friday Andy Burnham will travel to Brussels for a UK-EU summit to seal an agreement on closer ties with the bloc.

The Daily Express also leads on a potential bid for a Brexit reversal. It writes that campaigners are warning the prime minister that the UK would need to take in around 4,400 asylum seekers every year or pay £76m under the EU's asylum solidarity scheme. It also quotes Burnham as having recently said: \"Britain has 'lost more than we gained' in the decade since the referendum\".

The Times leads with NHS leaders warning the government that new laws banning zero-hours contracts could make it harder to hire health workers and provide emergency cover for fire services in emergencies. Public sector bodies are urging a re-think of the plans before they come into force next year. A government spokesperson said: \"We are committed to tackling the one-sided flexibility that can result from zero-hours and similar contracts\".

The Guardian says the prime minister has vowed early intervention to tackle the UK's youth joblessness crisis ahead of Alan Milburn's long-awaited report into the issue, to be released on Monday. Burnham's pledge includes more opportunities for vocational training in schools in a plan to help under-25s into employment and cut benefits bill.

The Metro headlines on the government considering \"a rethink on the age of consent\" in the UK to prevent adults having relationships with 16- and 17-year-olds. It comes as a woman who alleges she was raped by jailed comedian Russell Brand when she was 16 is now campaigning to see the law changed. Mia Latter is one of six women who made allegations against Brand in 2023 as part of a Times, Sunday Times and Channel 4's Dispatches investigation. Brand denied the allegations at the time and none of the six women were complainants in Brand's recent criminal trial, in which he was convicted of rape and sexual assault.

The i-Paper says there is \"mounting pressure\" from campaigners to change the law, adding that ministers are considering a new \"staggered\" age of consent. Currently, adults of any age are legally able to have sex with 16 and 17-year-olds under UK law.

The Sun covers Brand's wife, Laura Brand, reading a statement from her husband as she returned to the couple's podcast on Sunday. Brand has positioned himself as a Christian influencer, and has a large following among believers, including in the US.

The Financial Times writes that both democratic and republican lawmakers in the US have thrown support behind bills to crack down on advanced AI chips reaching China in the wake of Nvidia founder Jensen Huang's resignation, after revelations he allegedly had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has also called for an assessment of the chipmaker complying with export restrictions.

The Daily Mail reports that Home Office data indicates the government has spent nearly £80,000 a day on transporting asylum seekers. A Home Office spokesman told the paper: \"We have ended the unrestricted use of taxis and rooting out waste in the asylum system is a priority.\"

The Daily Mirror says soaring energy bills are taking a toll on terminally ill people and their families following a call for help on energy bills from charity Marie Curie.

The Daily Star's front teases a new study into gangland killings, including an interactive map of 1,000 cold-case crimes. It is also one of several papers to use a photo of Ezri Konsa celebrating after scoring the second goal for England in the Nations League. The team went on to win 3-2 against Spain.

The former Prime Minister Boris Johnson has told the Daily Telegraph that \"Britain would back Brexit again\" if the country was forced into another vote on the issue - and he has urged Andy Burnham not to waste his premiership on Europe.

But writing in the Daily Mirror, the prime minister says Johnson went for a much harder Brexit than the one promised at the referendum.

Citing figures from the campaign group Stay Out, the Daily Express says a Brexit U-turn would mean Britain could have to take in around 4,400 asylum seekers every year - or pay an annual bill of £76m.

The Times says NHS and fire service leaders have warned the government that banning zero-hours contracts will put the public at risk. They say it would be impossible to employ people as emergency cover, without guaranteeing them a certain number of hours or compensating them for late shift changes. A government spokesperson tells the paper it is considering responses to its consultation and working to get the detail right.

Writing in the Guardian, the prime minister pledges to intervene early in children's lives to tackle youth unemployment, promising \"a root-and-branch rethink of how we support childhood\". Burnham promises to intervene at all the stages of life in which young people fall behind, and \"long before they find themselves out of work and reliant on the state\".

The Sun quotes Reform UK, which argues that Labour's own tax rises have made it harder for businesses to hire young people.

Writing in the Times, the Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy says she's convening senior members of the entertainment and sports industries to discuss systems to identify abusers early - and she warns them if they don't act, she'll step in. She says she believes abuse is still happening now, and cases such as Russell Brand's should be a wake-up call for us as a country.

Sir David Beckham has \"kicked up a stink\" because his luxury perfumes are being distributed through the budget retailer Poundland, according to the Daily Mail. The paper says his lawyers are demanding more than £30m for associating his brand with cheap, discount products. The company that produces his fragrances, Coty, has denied selling them in Poundland - but says it has the right to decide where to sell the range.

England's football victory over Spain dominates the back pages. The Daily Mirror calls it a nerve-jangling classic. The Telegraph says it was a magical night in Madrid. The Mail calls it \"Spain relief.\" \"Vamos!\" is the i'Paper's headline.
